positiveFindings: Zero `any` types across all 93 component source files
Zero non-null assertions (`!`) in component source files (only in .stories.ts and .test.ts)
All custom events use typed CustomEvent<DetailType> with explicit detail interfaces
Union types used consistently for variant properties (no enums found)
All public methods have explicit return types
override render() consistently used across all components
9 components already use PropertyValues<this> correctly (status-indicator, switch, radio-group, slider, toggle-button, number-input)

typeAssertions.description: Usage of `as` type assertions instead of type guards or proper typing

findings.pattern: e.target as HTMLSlotElement in slotchange handlers
findings.description: Nearly every component casts e.target to HTMLSlotElement in slotchange event handlers. While this is a well-known Lit pattern and the cast is always correct in slotchange context, a type-safe helper function would be preferable.
findings.fix: Create a shared type guard: function isSlotChangeEvent(e: Event): e is Event & { target: HTMLSlotElement } { return e.target instanceof HTMLSlotElement; } -- or a shared utility: function getSlotTarget(e: Event): HTMLSlotElement { if (!(e.target instanceof HTMLSlotElement)) throw new Error('Expected slotchange target'); return e.target; }

findings.pattern: e.target as HTMLInputElement / HTMLTextAreaElement / HTMLSelectElement in form components
findings.description: Form components cast e.target to specific input element types in input/change handlers. These casts are correct in practice since the handlers are bound to shadow DOM <input>/<textarea>/<select> elements, but instanceof checks would be type-safe.
findings.fix: Use instanceof guard: const target = e.target; if (!(target instanceof HTMLInputElement)) return; // target is now narrowed to HTMLInputElement

findings.pattern: document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null
findings.description: Six components cast document.activeElement to HTMLElement. Since activeElement can be any Element (including SVGElement), this is an unsafe narrowing.
findings.current: const active = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
findings.fix: Use instanceof guard: const active = document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement ? document.activeElement : null;

findings.pattern: e.currentTarget as HTMLElement
findings.description: Components cast e.currentTarget to HTMLElement in pointer/mouse handlers. Since currentTarget is typed as EventTarget | null in the DOM spec, this needs narrowing.
findings.fix: Guard with instanceof: const target = e.currentTarget; if (target instanceof HTMLElement) { target.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); }

findings.pattern: slot.assignedElements()[0] as HTMLElement | undefined
findings.description: Components access the first assigned element of a slot and cast it. The array access with noUncheckedIndexedAccess would already return Element | undefined, but the cast to HTMLElement is the issue.
findings.current: const trigger = slot.assignedElements()[0] as HTMLElement | undefined;
findings.fix: const assigned = slot.assignedElements()[0]; const trigger = assigned instanceof HTMLElement ? assigned : undefined;

findings.pattern: e.composedPath()[0] as specific component type
findings.description: Accordion casts the first element of composedPath() to HelixAccordionItem without validation.
findings.fix: const target = e.composedPath()[0]; if (!(target instanceof HelixAccordionItem)) return; // target is now narrowed

findings.pattern: Floating-UI Placement type casting
findings.description: Components that use @floating-ui/dom cast their placement strings to the library's Placement type after string manipulation.
findings.fix: Create a typed mapping function: function toFloatingPlacement(p: DropdownPlacement): FloatingPlacement { const map: Record<DropdownPlacement, FloatingPlacement> = { start: 'left', end: 'right', ... }; return map[p] ?? p; }

findings.pattern: JSON.parse with unsafe cast
findings.description: data-table parses JSON strings and casts results directly without runtime validation.
findings.current: this.columns = JSON.parse(this.columns as unknown as string) as HxDataTableColumn[];
findings.fix: Parse to unknown first (which hx-nav and hx-split-panel already do correctly), then validate shape: const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(raw); if (Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.every(isHxDataTableColumn)) { this.columns = parsed; }

findings.pattern: HTMLElement & { disabled?: boolean } intersection cast
findings.description: Action bar casts elements to an intersection type to check for disabled property.
findings.current: const elWithDisabled = el as HTMLElement & { disabled?: boolean };
findings.fix: Use property check: function hasDisabled(el: HTMLElement): el is HTMLElement & { disabled: boolean } { return 'disabled' in el; }

findings.pattern: Form element type assertions in hx-form
findings.description: hx-form casts generic elements to HTMLInputElement, HTMLSelectElement, etc. for form validation methods.
findings.fix: Create type guard: function isValidatableElement(el: Element): el is HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement | HTMLTextAreaElement { return 'checkValidity' in el && typeof (el as Record<string, unknown>).checkValidity === 'function'; }

findings.pattern: e.target as HTMLElement in panel/overlay click handlers
findings.description: Components like dropdown, drawer, and breadcrumb cast e.target to HTMLElement in click handlers.
findings.fix: Guard: const target = e.target; if (!(target instanceof HTMLElement)) return;

missingGenericConstraints.description: Lifecycle methods using Map<string, unknown> or Map<PropertyKey, unknown> instead of PropertyValues<this>

findings.pattern: updated/willUpdate/firstUpdated using Map<string, unknown> instead of PropertyValues<this>
findings.description: 37 lifecycle method signatures use Map<string, unknown> or Map<PropertyKey, unknown> or Map<string | symbol, unknown> instead of the type-safe PropertyValues<this>. This loses all property name checking and value type inference. Only 9 components use the correct PropertyValues<this> type.
findings.fix: override updated(changedProperties: PropertyValues<this>): void { -- Import PropertyValues from 'lit' if not already imported. This enables type-safe changedProperties.has('propName') calls where propName is checked against actual component property names.

looseUnionTypes.description: Properties typed as `string` where a union type would be more appropriate

findings.pattern: language: string on hx-code-snippet
findings.description: The `language` property accepts any string but should be constrained to known syntax highlight language identifiers.
findings.fix: export type CodeLanguage = 'typescript' | 'javascript' | 'html' | 'css' | 'json' | 'python' | 'bash' | 'sql' | (string & Record<never, never>); // allows known autocomplete + arbitrary strings -- language: CodeLanguage = '';

findings.pattern: ariaLabel: string on hx-action-bar
findings.description: While string is correct for aria-label values, the default value is hardcoded rather than using undefined with a fallback.
findings.fix: No action needed -- string is correct for aria attributes. This is an informational finding only.

findings.pattern: button-group value setter casts string to union
findings.description: The orientation setter accepts string and casts to a union type inline.
findings.fix: Type the setter parameter as the union directly, or validate at the boundary: if (value !== 'horizontal' && value !== 'vertical') return;

typeWidening.description: Usage of overly wide types like Record<string, unknown>, Object, or loose generics

findings.pattern: rows: Record<string, unknown>[] on hx-data-table
findings.description: The data-table rows property uses Record<string, unknown>[] which provides no type safety for row data. While this is intentionally generic (table accepts arbitrary data), a generic type parameter would be more idiomatic.
findings.fix: Consider a generic approach or at minimum document the expected shape. For Lit components, generics on the class are complex, but the type could be narrowed: rows: Array<Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>> = []; -- Or provide a utility type: type DataTableRow = Record<string, unknown>;

findings.pattern: JSON.parse to Record<string, unknown>[] without validation
findings.description: Data table parses JSON attribute values with double-cast through unknown then to specific array types.
findings.current: this.rows = JSON.parse(this.rows as unknown as string) as Record<string, unknown>[];
findings.fix: Parse safely: const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(raw); if (Array.isArray(parsed)) { this.rows = parsed as Record<string, unknown>[]; } -- Better: validate each element has expected shape.

findings.pattern: Private _codeText typed as string with empty default
findings.description: Minor: private state uses loose string type where empty string initialization is fine but could use explicit type annotation.
findings.fix: No action needed -- string is correct here. Informational only.

findings.pattern: Form validation errors as Array<{ name: string; message: string }>
findings.description: The hx-form component repeats the error shape inline in multiple places instead of using a named interface.
findings.current: private _validationErrors: Array<{ name: string; message: string }> = [];
findings.fix: Extract to a named interface: export interface FormValidationError { name: string; message: string; } -- Then use: private _validationErrors: FormValidationError[] = [];

findings.pattern: hx-form checkValidity cast through Record<string, unknown>
findings.description: Form checks for checkValidity by casting to Record then checking typeof.
findings.fix: Use 'checkValidity' in el && typeof el.checkValidity === 'function' -- which narrows without requiring the Record cast.

inconsistentNullHandling.description: Inconsistent patterns for handling null/undefined values

findings.pattern: formStateRestoreCallback parameter type inconsistency
findings.description: Form-associated components have inconsistent parameter types for formStateRestoreCallback. Some accept (state: string), some accept (state: string | File | FormData | null, reason: string), and some accept (state: string | File | FormData). The spec defines the parameter as (state: File | string | FormData | null, reason: 'restore' | 'autocomplete').

affectedFiles.current: formStateRestoreCallback(state: string | File | FormData | null, _reason: string): void
formStateRestoreCallback(state: string | File | FormData | null, _reason: string): void

findings.fix: Standardize all implementations to match the spec: formStateRestoreCallback(state: File | string | FormData | null, _reason: 'restore' | 'autocomplete'): void { if (typeof state !== 'string') return; ... }

findings.pattern: Nullable query results accessed without null guard
findings.description: Some components use @query() which returns undefined when element is not found, but access properties on the result without explicit null checks. The current code uses optional chaining in most places correctly.
findings.fix: This is actually correct -- the undefined type annotation on @query is the right pattern, and the code does check for null before use. Informational finding.

missingReadonly.description: Mutable fields that should be readonly

findings.pattern: Static instance counters not marked readonly
findings.description: Components using static counters for unique ID generation have them marked as private but not readonly (which is correct since they increment). However, the generated ID fields could be readonly.
findings.fix: Mark the generated ID as readonly since it should never change after construction: private readonly _panelId = `hx-dropdown-panel-${++HelixDropdown._instanceCounter}`;

nonNullAssertions.note: Zero non-null assertions found in component source files (.ts). Non-null assertions exist only in .stories.ts and .test.ts files, which is acceptable at test boundaries.

implicitAny.description: Parameters or variables with implicit any type
implicitAny.note: Zero implicit any types found. TypeScript strict mode is properly enforced across all component source files.

missingReturnTypes.description: Public methods missing explicit return type annotations
missingReturnTypes.note: All public methods and lifecycle overrides have explicit return types. render() methods consistently return TemplateResult or use implicit return type inference (which is acceptable for Lit render()).

unsafeEventHandling.note: All custom events use typed CustomEvent<DetailType> with explicit detail interfaces. Event maps are well-typed across the library.

complianceScore.notes: The codebase demonstrates excellent TypeScript discipline with zero `any`, zero `@ts-ignore`, and zero non-null assertions in production code. The two main improvement areas are: (1) migrating 37 lifecycle methods from Map<string, unknown> to PropertyValues<this>, and (2) replacing ~89 type assertions with proper type guards via shared utility functions.
